title: 三角波电流通过电感
statement: 电流源 i_s 是对称三角波，峰值 I_m = 0.5 A，f = 1 kHz。t = 0 时它为零并上升，t = T/4 时达到 +0.5 A，3T/4 时为 −0.5 A。它的傅里叶级数为
i_s = \frac{8I_m}{π²}(sin ωt − \frac{1}{9}sin 3ωt + \frac{1}{25}sin 5ωt − …)，ω = 2π × 1000 rad/s（计算取到 99 次谐波）。
i_s 全部流过电感 L = 10 mH。求 i_L 的有效值和基波振幅。再求 v_L 的 3 次谐波振幅和基波初相，并判断 v_L 的波形。

questions.explain: 三角波的有效值 I = I_m/√3 = 0.5/√3 ≈ 0.2887 A。幅值相同的锯齿波也是这个值：两者都是线性变化的波形。

questions.ask: v_L 的 3 次谐波振幅 V_L3m = ?
v_L 基波的初相 = ?（cos 参考）
questions.explain: i_L 的基波 I_1m sin ωt = I_1m cos(ωt − 90°)，电感电压超前电流 90°，所以 v_L 基波初相为 0°。

choiceExplain: 正弦波只是 v_L 的基波；v_L 还含有各奇次谐波。
电感电压是电流的导数，三角波的导数不是三角波。
锯齿波含偶次谐波，而 i_L 半波对称、只有奇次谐波，导数也一样。
questions.explain: v_L = L di/dt：三角波每段的斜率是 ±4I_m/T，所以 v_L 在 ±L·4I_m f = ±10m × 4 × 0.5 × 1000 = ±20 V 之间跳变，是方波。从谐波看：V_Lkm = kωL·I_km ∝ k·(1/k²) = 1/k，正是方波的频谱。
方波的有效值等于幅值 20 V（取到 99 次谐波的级数给出 19.96 V）。

hints: 电流的各次谐波振幅直接从级数读出；有效值可以用三角波的定义求（v、i 线性变化的波形，有效值是峰值的 1/√3）。
电感对 k 次谐波的感抗是 kωL，电压超前电流 90°；所以 v_L 的 k 次谐波振幅是 kωL·I_km。
v_L = L di/dt：看三角波每一段的斜率，就能直接画出 v_L 的波形。
solution: **3. 波形。** V_Lkm ∝ k/k² = 1/k，与方波的频谱相同。直接用 v_L = L di/dt：上升段斜率 4I_m/T = 2000 A/s，v_L = 0.01 × 2000 = 20 V；下降段为 −20 V。v_L 是幅值 **20 V 的方波**，有效值 **20 V**。
**检查：** 方波基波振幅应为 4 × 20/π = 25.46 V，与第 2 步算出的 V_L1m 一致。

en.title: A triangle-wave current through an inductor
statement: The current source i_s is a symmetric triangle wave of peak I_m = 0.5 A and f = 1 kHz. It is zero and rising at t = 0, reaches +0.5 A at t = T/4 and −0.5 A at 3T/4. Its Fourier series is
i_s = \frac{8I_m}{π²}(sin ωt − \frac{1}{9}sin 3ωt + \frac{1}{25}sin 5ωt − …), ω = 2π × 1000 rad/s (harmonics up to the 99th are kept).

All of i_s flows through the inductor L = 10 mH. Find the rms value and the fundamental amplitude of i_L. Then find the 3rd-harmonic amplitude and the fundamental's initial phase of v_L, and identify the waveform of v_L.
hints: Read the current's harmonic amplitudes from the series; the rms value follows from the definition of a triangle wave (a linearly changing wave has rms = peak/√3).
At harmonic k the inductor's reactance is kωL and its voltage leads the current by 90°, so the k-th harmonic of v_L has amplitude kωL·I_km.
v_L = L di/dt: the slope of each segment of the triangle gives the waveform of v_L directly.
solution: **1. Current.** rms value I = I_m/√3 = **0.2887 A**; fundamental amplitude I_1m = 8I_m/π² = **0.4053 A**, 3rd-harmonic amplitude I_3m = I_1m/9 = 0.04503 A.
- fundamental: V_L1m = 62.83 × 0.4053 = 25.46 V; the current's fundamental has initial phase −90° (a sine), so leading by 90° the voltage's fundamental has initial phase **0°**;

**3. Waveform.** V_Lkm ∝ k/k² = 1/k, the spectrum of a square wave. Directly from v_L = L di/dt: the rising segment has slope 4I_m/T = 2000 A/s, v_L = 0.01 × 2000 = 20 V; the falling segment gives −20 V. v_L is a **20 V square wave** with rms value **20 V**.
**Check:** a square wave's fundamental has amplitude 4 × 20/π = 25.46 V, the same V_L1m as in step 2.

questions.explain: The rms value of a triangle wave is I = I_m/√3 = 0.5/√3 ≈ 0.2887 A. A sawtooth with the same peak has the same value: both change linearly.

questions.ask: Amplitude of the fundamental of i_L, I_1m = ?
Amplitude of the 3rd harmonic of v_L, V_L3m = ?
Initial phase of the fundamental of v_L = ? (cosine reference)
questions.explain: The fundamental of i_L is I_1m sin ωt = I_1m cos(ωt − 90°); the inductor voltage leads by 90°, so the fundamental of v_L has initial phase 0°.

questions.ask: What is the waveform of v_L?
choiceExplain: A sine wave is only the fundamental of v_L; v_L contains all the odd harmonics too.
The inductor voltage is the derivative of the current, and the derivative of a triangle is not a triangle.
A sawtooth contains even harmonics, while i_L has half-wave symmetry and only odd harmonics — and so does its derivative.
questions.explain: v_L = L di/dt: each segment of the triangle has slope ±4I_m/T, so v_L jumps between ±L·4I_m f = ±10m × 4 × 0.5 × 1000 = ±20 V — a square wave. In harmonic terms V_Lkm = kωL·I_km ∝ k·(1/k²) = 1/k, exactly the spectrum of a square wave.
A square wave's rms value equals its amplitude, 20 V (the series up to the 99th harmonic gives 19.96 V).
